tagline: Seven and a half miles of red rock into Sedona.
intro: Off the interstate at exit 298, State Route 179 turns north into the red rock country of the Coconino National Forest. It passes through the Village of Oak Creek, with the Bell Rock scenic area at the north end of town, then follows the east bank of Oak Creek into Sedona and crosses it just before the road ends. The whole drive is seven and a half miles.

The road was made an All-American Road in 2006 for the sandstone it runs through, a designation meant to say the road is a destination in itself. Sedona is named for Sedona Schnebly, whose mother said she made the name up because it sounded pretty.

moments.title: Bell Rock
moments.text: The butte stands just north of the Village of Oak Creek. A moderate hike reaches a small plateau on its northwest face, and the summit takes an unmarked trail.

moments.title: Cathedral Rock
moments.text: About a mile west of the road, it was called Court House Rock on early maps, and Courthouse Butte was called Church House Rock, which has caused endless confusion ever since.

moments.title: Chapel of the Holy Cross
moments.text: Looking at the site, the architects said nature had done everything and all they had to do was understate. Some 25 tons of rock were moved for it without dynamite.
